definition: no_unusual_action — a run against the earlier runs of its own case. With k of the m most recent earlier runs of the case (at most 20, newest first) doing a thing, its share is (k + 1) / (m + 2). A tool this run called is UNUSUAL when its share is a quarter or less (4 · (k + 1) ≤ m + 2), counting only earlier runs whose calls were recorded. The rule FAILS when at least one unusual tool may act. A tool is a look-up, and never counted, when the catalogue marks it readOnlyHint true, or, with no word from the catalogue, when its name split on - _ . or space holds a read token (read, get, list, search, find, fetch, query, view, show, cat, grep, head, tail, stat, ls, describe, lookup, select, count); a catalogue readOnlyHint of false makes it act whatever its name; a name that says nothing is taken to act. The rule SKIPS without tool calls; below three earlier runs with recorded calls (insufficient_history); and when more than half of the earlier runs each called a tool that may act and that is unusual against the other earlier runs (asked only when those others number three or more). A measurement: it reports and never decides the verdict. Positive = the run took an unusual action (the rule should FAIL).
source: Authored 2026-11-10. Synthetic histories chosen so every label follows from the count stated in the note: each line of the share table (m of 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 13, 14, 20) on both sides, the window of twenty, look-ups by name and by the catalogue, runs with no recorded calls, and a history with no usual way of going.
labelling: Labelled 2026-11-10 against the documented definition by counting, in a script that imports nothing from Iris: each note states how many of the earlier runs did the thing and the share the label follows from. A conformance family: it measures that the formula is implemented as written, not what a departure is worth. What a fire is worth is measured on AgentDojo runs and published in proof/OUTSIDE.md.
